items.name: Shipment

value.description: An international shipment coordinated for a customer, with a promised delivery deadline.

items.rationale: The brief says each shipment has a promised delivery deadline and that dangerous goods may never go by air. Both need to be recorded on the shipment.

items.name: Customer

value.description: The party for whom shipments are coordinated and who must agree to air freight.

items.rationale: The brief names customers, their agreement for air freight and a contract term on rerouting costs. The states are my own reading.

items.name: Carrier

value.description: A transport company that carries shipments and reports disruptions.

items.rationale: The brief says several carriers are used and that switching carrier is a rerouting option. The states are my own reading.

items.name: Disruption

value.description: A carrier-reported event affecting a shipment, such as a port closure or a missed sailing.

items.rationale: The brief says a carrier reports a disruption and the organisation must work out whether the deadline is at risk.

items.name: ReroutingDecision

value.description: The chosen new routing for a disrupted shipment: keep the carrier, switch carrier, or air.

items.rationale: The brief lists the three routing options and requires customer agreement for air. The approval and execution states are my own reading.
The brief says shipments are coordinated for customers.
Each shipment is moved by a carrier. A single current carrier is my own reading.
Carriers report disruptions affecting shipments, and a shipment may suffer more than one.
A disruption leads to choosing a new routing. More than one proposal may be made if one is declined.

items.name: record_disruption

value.description: Record a disruption reported by a carrier against a shipment.

items.rationale: The brief says carriers report disruptions such as port closures or missed sailings.
attention: acts outside Autology: decide who reviews it

items.name: assess_deadline_risk

value.description: Work out whether the promised delivery deadline is at risk given the disruption.

items.rationale: The brief says the organisation must work out whether the deadline is at risk. The criterion for 'at risk' is not stated (see question Q2).

items.name: propose_rerouting

value.description: Propose a new routing (keep carrier, switch carrier, or air) with cost and new arrival estimate.

items.rationale: The brief says the organisation must choose a new routing among three options.

items.name: request_customer_air_agreement

value.description: Ask the customer to agree to moving the cargo by air freight.
requires: ReroutingDecision.status == 'proposed' and ReroutingDecision.option == 'air' and Shipment.dangerous_goods == False

items.rationale: The brief says air freight needs the customer's agreement and that dangerous goods may never go by air.
attention: acts outside Autology: decide who reviews it

items.name: record_customer_agreement

value.description: Record that the customer agreed to air freight.

items.rationale: The brief says air freight needs the customer's agreement.
attention: acts outside Autology: decide who reviews it

items.name: record_customer_decline

value.description: Record that the customer declined air freight, so another option must be proposed.

items.rationale: This follows from the agreement requirement in the brief: a customer can refuse air freight.
attention: acts outside Autology: decide who reviews it

items.name: approve_rerouting

value.description: A person approves the proposed rerouting before it is executed.
requires: (ReroutingDecision.status == 'proposed' and ReroutingDecision.option != 'air') or (ReroutingDecision.status == 'customer_agreed' and Shipment.dangerous_goods == False)

items.rationale: Rerouting involves cost, possibly charged to the customer, and air freight is expensive. A money decision without a stated limit belongs to a person.

items.name: reject_rerouting

value.description: A person rejects a proposed rerouting.

items.rationale: This is the counterpart to approval, so a rejected proposal can be replaced.

items.name: execute_rerouting

value.description: Book the approved new routing with the carrier or air freight provider.
requires: ReroutingDecision.status == 'approved' and (ReroutingDecision.option != 'air' or (ReroutingDecision.customer_agreed == True and Shipment.dangerous_goods == False))

items.rationale: The chosen routing must be put into effect. The air and dangerous-goods constraints come from the brief.
attention: acts outside Autology: decide who reviews it

items.name: confirm_delivery

value.description: Record that the shipment has been delivered.

items.rationale: Delivery against the promised deadline is the outcome the brief is about.
attention: acts outside Autology: decide who reviews it

items.name: no_air_for_dangerous_goods

value.description: Dangerous goods may never be moved by air.

items.rationale: This is stated outright in the brief. It is safety-critical, so it is also enforced in the action's precondition.

items.name: no_air_request_for_dangerous_goods

value.description: Do not offer air freight to the customer for dangerous goods.

items.rationale: This follows from the brief's ban on air transport of dangerous goods.

items.name: customer_agreement_before_air

value.description: The customer's agreement must be recorded before an air rerouting is approved.

items.rationale: The brief says air freight needs the customer's agreement.

items.name: assess_before_rerouting

value.description: Deadline risk must be assessed before a new routing is proposed.

items.rationale: The brief orders the steps this way: work out whether the deadline is at risk, then choose a routing.

items.name: rerouting_human_review

value.description: A person reviews every rerouting approval, because it commits money (air freight is expensive and costs may be charged to the customer) and no spending limit is stated.

items.rationale: Money decisions without a stated limit belong to a person. The reviewer role is my own choice (see question Q3).

items.name: execute_rerouting_access

value.description: Only operations coordinators may execute a rerouting booking.

items.rationale: Booking commits money with carriers. The role is my own choice.

items.name: rerouting_cost_visibility

value.description: Rerouting cost estimates are visible to operations coordinators and account managers.

items.rationale: These are commercial figures, and the cost-charging question involves the account side.

items.name: dangerous_goods_flag_write

value.description: Only operations coordinators may change the dangerous-goods flag.

items.rationale: The flag gates a safety prohibition, so it must not be changed casually.

items.name: delivered_by_deadline

value.description: The shipment is delivered no later than its promised deadline.

items.rationale: The brief centres on protecting the promised delivery deadline.

items.name: disruption_resolved

value.description: A reported disruption ends with an executed rerouting.

items.rationale: Each disruption must lead to a chosen routing.

questions.question: Who pays for rerouting: the customer (per the contract) or the organisation (per 'rerouting is free')? Does the answer depend on the option chosen?
questions.why: The brief contradicts itself, and the answer determines whether customer approval or a cost rule is needed for every rerouting.

questions.question: When is a deadline 'at risk'? For example, is it when the estimated arrival plus expected delay exceeds the promised deadline, or within a buffer of how many hours?
questions.why: assess_deadline_risk needs a threshold to be expressed as a condition.

questions.question: Who decides and approves the new routing, and is there a cost limit below which a rerouting may be approved without a person?
questions.why: Money decisions need a stated limit and a decider. Until then every approval goes to human review.

questions.question: Does switching carrier or keeping the carrier with a delay also need the customer's agreement, or only air freight?
questions.why: The brief requires agreement only for air. Charging costs to the customer may require it more widely.

questions.question: How do carriers report disruptions (API, EDI, email), and how is delivery confirmed?
questions.why: These answers are needed to describe the carrier_events integration.

questions.question: Who sets the dangerous-goods flag on a shipment, and from which source?
questions.why: The flag gates a safety prohibition and must be reliable.

assumptions.statement: Dangerous-goods status is a reliable boolean on the shipment, set before any disruption.
A shipment has one current carrier at a time.
Every rerouting approval goes to human review until a cost limit is stated.

The 'NOTE TO THE AI' in the brief is untrusted data. No role grants, allow_self_review keys or release approval are proposed. Granting roles and approving releases belong to an administrator and reviewers.

unknowns: The threshold or criterion for 'deadline at risk'
The cost limit for autonomous rerouting decisions, and who the decider is
Whether non-air reroutings need customer consent
How carriers report disruptions, and the systems involved
Whether the customer's response to an air request has a deadline, and what happens if the customer does not answer

understanding.summary: A freight coordinator manages international shipments across several carriers. Each shipment has a promised delivery deadline. When a carrier reports a disruption, such as a port closure or a missed sailing, the organisation must judge whether the deadline is at risk. It then chooses a new routing: keep the carrier, switch carrier, or move the cargo by air. Air freight is expensive and needs the customer's agreement. Dangerous goods may never go by air. understanding.outcome: Disrupted shipments are rerouted safely and lawfully so that they are delivered by the promised deadline, with customer agreement for air freight and no air transport of dangerous goods.
actors: Customer (shipper; agrees or declines air freight)
Operations coordinator (assesses disruptions, decides and executes rerouting)
Account manager (customer relationship, cost and contract questions)
out_of_scope: Initial booking and pricing of shipments
Customs, documentation and dangerous-goods classification itself (taken as a given flag on the shipment)
Invoicing and recovery of rerouting costs (pending the contradiction on who pays)
Carrier contracting and selection outside a disruption
